Vocabulary & Grammar. The wording is correct and free of errors. <5>/5  
Text-Based Answerability. The text confirms both “went to the market” and “tried local food”, so the answer is only partially supported; the test‑taker must choose between two correct statements. <3>/5  
Reading Dependency. Without reading, a guesser might pick any activity typical of a holiday, so the answer is not easily guessable. <4>/5  
Answer Unambiguity. Because more than one option is accurate, the correct answer is not unambiguous. <1>/5  
Distractor Plausibility. All three options are plausible actions described in the passage, which is appropriate for distractors. <5>/5  
Using Paraphrases. The correct choice (“Went to the market”) repeats the wording from the text rather than paraphrasing it. <2>/5  
Explanation Quality. No explanation was supplied for this item, so it fails to justify the correct answer or dismiss the distractors. <1>/5

Text Coverage. The three questions focus almost exclusively on the market episode and the fruit warning, neglecting other parts of the story (e.g., the locals’ interaction, Mark’s emotional change). <2>/5
